Two grafts: from Fixed-Frame Kappa-Ball, define the shell measure phi on the RETRACTION-SUBSET geometry, because the MPDAG covering relation has no known graphical characterisation and there is therefore no procedure that samples uniformly from a covering-graph shell — every other protocol that promises uniform shell sampling has promised something unimplementable; and from Oracle Meter v2, the fourth sentinel NO_RETRACTABLE_EDGES, distinct from UNREACHED, without which a vacuous-knowledge arm and a maximally robust one print the same value.

Every protocol here removes the 1,839.78 s enumerating validity predicate from the ball, and that is table stakes. Only this one identifies the SECOND exponential as the admission criterion rather than a cost. The mechanism is mechanical and the consequence is fatal to any protocol that does not fix it first — incomplete knowledge leaves undirected edges in G0, extensions then disagree, and the instance is deleted, so the pipeline systematically removes exactly the deployments the framework exists to serve and a realistic sparse elicited K yields an empty population. ranking: Oracle Meter v2 — taint-propagated deployment with a masked-compelled-edge bridge

axis_winners.why: Its four-tier split separates pedagogical drawings from fitted and applied networks, and the reason is measured rather than stylistic. I verified it: of the 831 admissible instances, all 16 with r >= 5 sit in `paths`, a 17-node dagitty illustration whose CPDAG is 73.7% undirected with a single 15-node chain component, and which supplies 20 of 831 instances and 13 of the 126 law exceptions. Remove the three illustrations and the maximum radius over 807 instances is 4, with 94.4% at r <= 2 and zero instances at r >= 5. So the sentence in circulation, that real structure reaches radius 14 against a synthetic maximum of 4 or 5, compares two designed spines, and on the corrected reading the real corpus minus one textbook drawing has a SMALLER maximum radius than the random generators. Its illustration gate makes reporting max radius twice, with and without T0, a standing rule. Runner-up is Oracle Meter v2, whose size-coverage correction (the existing ER sweep tops out at n=30, which reaches only 46.2% of admissible instance mass, against 82.7% at n<=50) and M-bias-as-latent-expansion recovery are both right and both verified.

Two decisions no other protocol makes. First, Y is drawn from possde(X, C-hat), never possde(X, G0), because G0 = Meek(C-hat, K) is knowledge-dependent, so a G0-based frame hands every knowledge arm a different candidate set, the paired instances stop being paired, and the K-empty arm gets the largest frame and the smallest yield. Four of the six protocols write the G0 version and then claim byte-identical instance sets across arms, which their own frame cannot deliver. Second, the fixed denominator: every K-dependent condition stops being a filter and becomes a per-instance status on one frozen list, printed as a composition column. That is the ledger's non-comparable-strata rule turned into a mechanism instead of a warning. Runner-up is Buy the Gate's common-support rule, which is the sharpest refinement available: the support is defined by the OBSERVABLE sources only, because letting an oracle source help define it readmits the truth into the deployment population through the back door.

The brief's single hardest fact is that no published study measures expert per-edge error against a known-true DAG, so the referent must be BUILT. Four Answerers is the only protocol that builds it: one frozen, hashed, observables-scoped questionnaire (424 questions over 29 networks, re-derived from C-hat rather than from what a true-DAG gate happened to admit) answered by published authors, a recruited human analyst round sized off a Wilson curve, an LLM in three naming conditions across two model families, and the mechanical generators. Everything else on the board substitutes a surrogate for the referent and then measures the surrogate. It also declares honestly that the human round measures analysts reading a data dictionary, not domain experts, which is the deployed case and the claim it can actually license. Two elements from elsewhere belong in the winner: Fixed-Frame's kappa-hat_split, the pairwise disagreement rate between two independent elicitations, which is an observable error floor requiring no truth and therefore exists on the sub-population where every truth-based referent and the incumbent test are both unavailable; and Three Denominators' randomised node-presentation order under a recorded seed, without which a positive graph-space clustering result cannot be separated from prompt-position bias.

It is the only protocol that noticed the radius may not be counted in the unit its own headline needs, and I confirmed both mechanisms in the source. retractable_edges returns edges directed in G0 and undirected in C-hat, so k_g0 counts asserted PLUS Meek-compelled edges; local_up_covers generates candidates by un-orienting one knowledge edge and re-closing, then keeps only the minimal ones, so one retraction can cost more than one BFS hop. Three distinct objects (r_hop, r_edge, r_claim), and the audit statement 'you may be wrong about up to r-1 of your own claims' needs the third. The committed data already show the units disagreeing: the radius exceeds min(s, |K_G0|) in 110 of 463 instances, with shapes up to r=14 against min=6. The predicted direction, r_claim <= r_edge <= r_hop, points the same optimistic way as the open Anti-Exchange Case B caveat, so two known one-sided errors compound. Runner-up is Fixed-Frame's shell measure, which is the only implementable one: it defines phi on j-subsets of K, states in writing that a uniform draw from a covering-graph shell cannot be written because the MPDAG covering relation has no known graphical characterisation, and promotes the O*-relevance weighting into the slot the competing paper declares empty.

Lever 0 is the correct diagnosis and the correct fix, and it is the only one on the board. optimal_adjustment_set_mpdag computes the DAG-level optimal set in EVERY extension and returns None on disagreement, which makes it population-shaping rather than merely slow: g0_undirected_edges is 0 in all 831 admissible instances, and all 518 o_g0_not_identified rejections fall at coverage 0.25 and 0.5 with zero at 1.0. Incomplete knowledge leaves undirected edges, extensions disagree, the instance is deleted, so the pipeline systematically removes exactly the analysts the framework is for. A realistic sparse K yields an empty population on current code, and no other protocol's A3 can run until this lands. Two elements from elsewhere complete it: Buy the Gate's failure-witness plus GAC-certificate pair with an explicit CENSORED verdict, which makes the cheap gate sound rather than merely fast and errs only in the direction that under-estimates r; and Four Answerers' measured cost curve, which I reproduced (sachs 336 extensions in 1.374 s at 17 undirected edges, insurance 41 in 7.198 s at 18) and which is the only empirical basis anyone offers for a cap value. One thing no protocol caught: local_up_covers itself calls enumerate_dag_extensions on every candidate to test minimality, so the cover generation is exponential in G0's undirected count too, and every timing in the tree was taken at zero.

It is the only protocol whose calibration statistic is checked for vacuity before it runs. The credibility ratio r / (kappa x |K_G0|) is arithmetically dead on data already on disk, because r = 1 in 61.1% of instances and median |K_G0| = 12, so the ratio falls below 1 for any kappa above 8.3% and no plausible expert error rate is under that. The replacement is the breach probability pi-hat = 1 - (1 - kappa)^r, denominated in assertions the analyst actually made, measured over the neighbourhood the radius reaches because O* is local, and resampled from the measured clustering of wrong assertions rather than assumed independent. At r = 1 and kappa = 0.10 it reads 0.10, which cannot saturate by construction and is a number a practitioner can act on. Paired with kappa-hat_split it is the Cinelli and Hazlett move executed on a referent computed from the analyst's own materials, available on the sub-population where G0 admits exactly one valid adjustment set and the incumbent test has no power at all. Runner-up, and it should be grafted: Three Denominators' 5x4 taxonomy, which turns the licensed narrow claim against Su and Henckel into a measured denominator (the BENIGN and EFFICIENCY column IS the untestable class) instead of an asserted scope limit.

objections.objection: THE VACUITY GATE IS DENOMINATED IN THE ONE FREE STATISTIC ALREADY MEASURED TO BE NON-PREDICTIVE, AND THE STRONGEST FREE PREDICTOR IS COMPUTED AND THEN EXCLUDED FROM THE RULE THAT COULD RETIRE THE FRAMEWORK. Fixed-Frame splits H4 into C-COUNT-A (|K|) and C-COUNT-B (|K_G0|) and writes the retirement rule as 'if either count baseline reproduces the radius's decision at every operating point of the audit arm's three-bucket score, the framework is retired to a lemma about counting'. Recomputed from results/axisa3/instances.jsonl: |K_G0| as the code writes it is exactly |retractable_edges(C-hat, G0)|, the same alphabet radius_local_up retracts from, so r <= |K_G0| is DEFINITIONAL, holding in 831 of 831 admissible instances, and it is a loose ceiling, with r = |K_G0| in only 15 of 831 (1.8%). Its rank correlation with r is 0.057 over all 831 (p = 0.102, indistinguishable from zero) and 0.118 on the 463 measurable. The retirement rule is therefore attached to a quantity that cannot win. Meanwhile separation, a plain BFS in C-hat from X to the nearest member of Z inside X's chain component (measure.py:136, fifteen lines, O(V+E), and Z = O(G0) is already on the deployment path), has rank correlation 0.695 with r (p = 4.6e-68). Fixed-Frame does compute min(s, |K_G0|) inside the check text, but the decision rule says 'either COUNT baseline', so the only predictor with any power is calculated and then held outside the rule. Worse, min(s, |K_G0|) = s in 463 of 463 measurable instances: |K_G0| never binds in the law the protocol cites as its evidence, so the 'count baseline' contributes literally nothing to it. Finally the quantifier makes the rule unfireable: 'at every operating point' means one disagreeing instance preserves the framework, which on a corpus with 195 disagreements is guaranteed.
objections.where: A3 falsifiable_check (a); arms C-COUNT-A and C-COUNT-B; primary_table Block 2 column 11; and the 'what it would show if the framework is wrong' item (3), which is also written only in counts
objections.repair: Replace the two count arms with a FREE-STATISTIC LADDER scored on one audited outcome over one instance set: B0 majority / certify-always; B1 component_size(X, C-hat), which is knowledge-free and known at frame-construction time; B2 the two-line rule (predict s where separation is measured, predict 1 where it is not); B3 min(s, |K_G0|); B4 |K_G0|; B5 |K|; B6 r. Replace the universal-quantifier rule with a pre-registered EQUIVALENCE margin on a paired within-instance contrast against B2, not against B4 or B5, with three declared verdicts: radius wins, equivalent, or UNDERPOWERED, and the UNDERPOWERED verdict pre-committed so that an interval wider than the margin can never be read as a win. Each baseline gets a declared decision rule and a swept threshold, so 'operating point' means an ROC and not a phrase.
objections.settling_measurement: Score B0 through B6 on the 831 committed instances today, at zero new compute, with the arm flag set to audit because that population's K is oracle-derived. Report the paired AUC difference B6 minus B2 on the audited three-bucket outcome with a cluster bootstrap over the 25 yielding networks, plus exact-value agreement per baseline. Repeat the identical ladder on the five-network D-LLM pilot that A2 already runs for its 40% admissibility gate, before the remaining elicitation budget is released.

objections.objection: THE POPULATION ON WHICH THE RADIUS SAYS ANYTHING A FREE BFS DOES NOT SAY, BY MORE THAN ONE, IS 18 INSTANCES ON 3 NETWORKS, AND 13 OF THEM SIT IN THE ONE TEXTBOOK DRAWING THE PROTOCOL'S OWN ILLUSTRATION GATE REMOVES FROM EVERY HEADLINE. Recomputed on the committed corpus: the two-line free rule (s where separation is measured, 1 where it is not) reproduces the radius EXACTLY on 636 of 831 instances (76.5%), 77.4% outside T0, 81.3% network-weighted, and on every single instance of 10 of the 25 yielding networks (Acid_1996, Didelez_2010, Sebastiani_2005, arth150, child, diabetes, ecoli70, hepar2, mediator, munin1; 212 instances, no errors). Within one, it reproduces 813 of 831 (97.8%) and 99.4% outside T0, on a certificate whose entire measured range outside T0 is {1,2,3,4} with 94.4% at r <= 2. Of the 126 law exceptions the protocol quotes as proof the baseline is not trivially right, 108 are off by exactly one. The set where |r minus free| >= 2 is 18 instances over 3 networks: paths 13, Kampen_2014 3, insurance 2. Fixed-Frame's own A1 illustration gate removes paths from every headline, which leaves FIVE instances on TWO networks as the entire evidence base for the geometry contributing something a hop count does not. Even the knowledge-free statistic is strong: component_size alone, computable from C-hat before any elicitation, classifies r = 1 against r >= 2 at 78.0% against a 61.1% majority baseline, and component_size = 2 gives r = 1 in 169 of 169. The two gates that jointly kill the framework, the illustration gate in A1 and the count baseline in A3, sit on different axes and neither reads the other.

objections.repair: Add a pre-registered RESCUE CLAUSE to the ladder: the radius survives the equivalence test only if the sub-population where it and B2 disagree by 2 or more (i) contains enough independent networks for a cluster-bootstrapped verdict, with the floor stated in advance, and (ii) carries the audited three-bucket outcome differently from the agreement sub-population. Compute the rescue set with and without T0 and print both, exactly as the illustration gate already prints max radius twice. Pre-register the fallback sentence: if the rescue set outside T0 is under the stated floor, the paper reports that on this substrate the certificate is an exact re-derivation of a hop count and the contribution narrows to phi plus the calibration plus the geometry.
objections.settling_measurement: The disagreement-set census, on the committed 831 today and again on the elicited-K pilot: n, number of distinct networks, the distribution of |r minus B2|, and the audited outcome rate inside and outside the disagreement set, each reported with and without T0. It costs one script and answers before any elicitation is bought.

objections.objection: PI-HAT, THE FLAGSHIP PRACTITIONER-FACING NUMBER, IS A MONOTONE FUNCTION OF r AND EQUALS KAPPA EXACTLY ON 61.1% OF THE CORPUS, AND ITS INFORMATIVENESS TEST IS PASSED BY VARIATION IN THE ELICITATION DISAGREEMENT RATE ALONE. The breach probability is pi-hat = 1 minus (1 minus kappa)^r. At r = 1 this is kappa, with no contribution from the geometry whatever, and r = 1 in 508 of 831 instances (61.1%; 503 of 807, 62.3%, outside T0). r is in {1,2} on 92.4% of the corpus and 94.4% outside T0, so pi-hat takes essentially two values, kappa and 2kappa minus kappa squared, across the non-illustration corpus, and the exponent that chooses between them is 82.6% predicted by the free binary rule 'is separation 1 or undefined'. Fixed-Frame's THIRD RULE says the informative outcome is a spread with neither tail holding more than 90%. That test is satisfied outright by between-network variation in kappa-hat_split with r held at 1 throughout, so it cannot distinguish 'the certificate carries information' from 'elicitation reliability varies by network', which is a fact about the surrogate and not about the framework. The protocol also contradicts itself here: A6 justifies measuring kappa LOCALLY on the grounds that 'the radius equalled the separation in 792 of 792 designed instances', so it treats r = s as true enough to determine where the referent is measured, while never registering r = s as the baseline that could retire it. If r = s the flagship number is 1 minus (1 minus kappa)^s: two free inputs, a BFS and two elicitations, and no radius.
objections.where: A6 decision (the breach probability replacing the credibility ratio); primary_table Block 1 column 9; A6 falsifiable_check THIRD RULE; and A6's own justification for local kappa
objections.repair: Restate the spread test CONDITIONAL ON r: report pi-hat's between-instance variance at fixed r and require it to exceed what kappa's between-network variance alone produces at that r. Add the paired competitor pi-hat(B2) = 1 minus (1 minus kappa)^s computed on the same instances, and pre-register the margin at which the radius's exponent earns its place, including the share of instances where the two disagree about crossing the 0.5 threshold column 9 already uses. Print kappa-hat_split and r as separate columns immediately beside pi-hat so a reader can see which input moved.
objections.settling_measurement: On the pilot's five networks under D-LLM, compute pi-hat(r) and pi-hat(B2) on identical instances and report the paired difference, the threshold-crossing disagreement rate at 0.5, and the variance decomposition of pi-hat into a between-network kappa component and a within-network r component.

objections.objection: D-NULL CANNOT PRODUCE A RADIUS, SO THE ARM WHOSE ENTIRE JOB IS TO SEPARATE 'THE RADIUS IS LARGE' FROM 'THE KNOWLEDGE WAS VACUOUS' IS ITSELF VACUOUS BY CONSTRUCTION. Verified in code: retractable_edges(cpdag, g) keeps edges directed in g and undirected in the CPDAG, so with K empty and G0 = C-hat the retractable set is empty, local_up_covers returns [], and radius_local_up exhausts its frontier immediately and returns UNREACHED with exact = True. D-NULL's radius column is therefore 100% UNREACHED sentinels on every instance, and Fixed-Frame's own sentinel discipline forbids averaging or plotting them. The protocol states D-NULL's purpose as separating a large radius from vacuous knowledge and then says its value is 'its enormous O-unidentified status count', which is a statement about identification and answers a different question. The result is that the leader has no chance-level anchor at all: its D-TRUE arm is matched on |K| and placement and is the CORRECTNESS control, but there is no arm holding cardinality and placement fixed while removing domain content, which is precisely the comparison the vacuity charge demands.
objections.where: arms, D-NULL; primary_table Block 1 column 5 (share UNREACHED) and column 3 (share at r = 1), both of which are undefined for that arm
objections.repair: Redefine the vacuity control as a size- and placement-matched RANDOM CONSISTENT K: same |K|, same granularity mix, same distance-from-X histogram as the D-LLM draw on that instance, orientations drawn uniformly among Meek-consistent choices on C-hat's undirected edges, redrawn on FAIL under a declared retry cap with cap-exceeded recorded as its own status. Keep K empty as a DEGENERATE REFERENCE reported as a status line, never as a radius row. This is the anchor that separates 'the radius is large because K is big and well placed' from 'because K is right', and it is the only arm that makes the D-LLM row a measurement of knowledge rather than of cardinality.
objections.settling_measurement: Paired radius-distribution comparison D-LLM against the matched-random arm on the frozen frame at matched |K_G0|, reported on the pre-declared summary (share at r = 1, median, max) with the sign and a cluster bootstrap over networks. If the two are not distinguishable, the radius measures how much was asserted and where, both of which are free.

objections.objection: THE CERTIFICATE LEDGER CARRIES NO |K_G0| COLUMN, NO SEPARATION COLUMN AND NO APPLICABILITY FUNNEL, SO NO ROW CAN BE READ FOR THE CONFOUND THE WHOLE ATTACK IS ABOUT. Because r <= |K_G0| is definitional, any cross-arm radius comparison at unmatched |K_G0| is partly a comparison of how much was asserted. Fixed-Frame matches D-TRUE to D-LLM on |K| and the distance histogram, which is correct, but D-PUB, D-SYN, D-NULL, A-ORACLE, N-ER-MATCHED and every substrate tier are unmatched, and the primary table prints neither |K_G0| nor separation anywhere in its sixteen columns. A referee cannot tell whether the D-PUB row differs from D-LLM because the papers asserted less or because they asserted better. The committed corpus already sizes the effect: median |K_G0| moves 12, 6, 4 across the coverage strata while max radius moves 14, 4, 4 with it. The vacuity denominator is likewise absent from the headline: the substrate section prints the undirected fraction per network, but the ledger's own rows carry no funnel, so the fact that the framework applies to 767 of 9,771 edges (7.85%) and 969 of 7,062 nodes (13.7%) across 276 chain components, on 25 of 39 networks, with 6 networks having nothing to orient at all, never travels with a number a reader will quote.
objections.where: primary_table Block 1, column ordering; and the substrate section, whose funnel statistics are printed once and never attached to a row
objections.repair: Insert two columns BEFORE column 3: |K_G0| median with IQR, and the separation composition as a three-level count (undefined / 1 / >= 2) with the undefined rate printed in the same cell. Add a per-tier funnel header to the ledger: nodes inside a chain component over total nodes, orientable edges over total edges, networks yielding any instance over networks parsed. Stratify every cross-arm headline by |K_G0| decile and print the within-stratum contrast beside the pooled one.
objections.settling_measurement: Recompute every cross-arm radius gap within |K_G0| deciles. If the gap vanishes inside strata, the row difference is cardinality and the sentence must be restated in those words. The stratified table is computable on the committed 831 immediately and costs nothing.

objections.objection: NOTHING IN THE PROTOCOL SEQUENCES THE BASELINE BEFORE THE SPEND, AND THE BASELINE IS THE CHEAPEST ITEM ON THE ENTIRE BOARD. The full free-statistic ladder runs on 831 rows already committed to the tree, in minutes, with zero new compute and zero model calls. Fixed-Frame's total_budget lists implementation items with no ordering and commits roughly 2,000 to 2,400 cached elicitations, about 22 human-hours of page-anchored adjudication and 55 to 70 agent-hours before the question that can retire the framework is answered, and the answer arrives as column 11 of a table written after the money is spent. The only pre-spend gate the protocol has is A2's admissibility pilot (fewer than 40% at status ok on five networks stops the run), which asks whether the population exists and never asks whether the answer is free. Every rival on the board sequences a blocking gate first, whether a week-one prior-art go / no-go, a unit reconciliation on committed data, a lever-zero admission check, or a stage-zero pilot. The leader's own strongest instinct, hunting down the illustration finding before writing the headline, is exactly the instinct it fails to apply to its own baseline.
objections.where: total_budget (no stated ordering); A3 falsifiable_check (a) as a reported column rather than a gate; A2's pilot gate, which is the only pre-spend checkpoint and asks a different question
objections.repair: Promote the ladder to STAGE 0, blocking and ordered before any elicitation budget is released: (i) run B0 through B6 on the 831 committed instances, flagged arm = audit because that K is oracle-derived; (ii) run the identical ladder on the five-network D-LLM pilot alongside the existing 40% admissibility gate, since both need the same pilot elicitation and neither needs the full corpus; (iii) publish the disagreement-set census with and without T0; (iv) release the remaining budget only on a stage-0 verdict of 'radius wins' or 'underpowered, and here is the instance count that would resolve it'.
objections.settling_measurement: The stage-0 report itself: per-baseline exact agreement, the paired AUC difference against B2 with a network-cluster bootstrap, the rescue-set size and its network count, all reported twice, with and without T0, and all before a single elicitation call is billed.

objections.objection: THE EVIDENCE THE PROTOCOL CITES TO ARGUE THE BASELINE IS NOT TRIVIALLY RIGHT IS DRAWN FROM THE COVERAGE STRATUM WHERE THE COUNT IS LOOSEST, AND BOTH FREE STATISTICS GET CLOSER TO r, NOT FURTHER, IN THE SPARSE REGIME THE PROTOCOL IS ACTUALLY DESIGNED FOR. Fixed-Frame's justification rests on the law block computed over the committed corpus, which is dominated by the coverage-1.0 stratum where G0 IS the true DAG and |K_G0| is large. Recomputed per stratum: the rank correlation of r with |K_G0| is 0.021 at coverage 1.0 (n = 543), 0.411 at coverage 0.5 (n = 182) and 0.508 at coverage 0.25 (n = 106), while median |K_G0| falls 12, 6, 4 and max radius falls 14, 4, 4. On the measurable subsets, r = s rises from 0.659 at coverage 1.0 to 0.876 at 0.5 and 0.845 at 0.25. So the ceiling tightens and the hop count sharpens as knowledge gets sparser, and sparse is exactly what an elicited K_LLM or a harvested K_PUB will produce. The protocol's one piece of prior evidence that the baseline cannot win is measured in the regime least like deployment, and it points the wrong way for the regime that matters. Fixed-Frame also mis-states that evidence: it writes that min(s, |K_G0|) 'is neither an upper bound nor a deterministic predictor', but r exceeds |K_G0| in ZERO of 831 instances, so the |K_G0| half is an upper bound universally and every one of the 110 exceptions is on the separation side. The pre-registered 'contradiction to resolve' is already half resolved, and it resolves against the protocol.
objections.where: A3 falsifiable_check (a), the sentence beginning 'There is prior evidence the baseline is not trivially right'
objections.repair: Pre-register the ladder separately within |K_G0| strata, and state the direction before the run: the free ladder's advantage is predicted to GROW as |K_G0| falls, so a confirming result cannot be reported as a surprise and a disconfirming one is a real update. Correct the cited evidence in the pre-registration: r <= |K_G0| holds in 831 of 831 and is definitional; the exceptions are r > s and belong to the separation baseline, not the count baseline. Report the ladder on the pilot's REALISED |K_G0| distribution rather than on the corpus's.
objections.settling_measurement: The ladder computed within |K_G0| deciles on the committed corpus, available now, plus the same decile table on the pilot's elicited K, with the pre-registered direction printed beside the result.

objections.objection: PHI, THE SECOND NUMBER OF THE TWO-NUMBER CERTIFICATE, CARRIES THE COUNT BASELINE IN ITS DENOMINATOR, SO ITS OWN INFORMATIVENESS TEST CAN BE PASSED BY |K_G0| VARIATION ALONE. phi_j is the fraction of j-subsets of K_G0 whose retraction invalidates Z. On the 61.1% of instances at r = 1, phi_r = phi_1 is (number of single retractions that break) over |K_G0|, and |K_G0| has median 10 and maximum 122 across the corpus, so phi_1 varies by an order of magnitude from its denominator before any geometry enters. Fixed-Frame's SHELL-INFORMATIVENESS check drops phi to an appendix if its interquartile range at fixed r is below 0.05, which conditions on r but not on cardinality, so a healthy spread is producible purely by how many claims each analyst made, which is the very baseline the protocol says it is testing against.
objections.where: A4 decision (shell measure) and A4 falsifiable_check (d); primary_table Block 1 column 6
objections.repair: Condition the informativeness test on (r, |K_G0|) jointly rather than on r alone. Report phi_1 against its trivial predictor 1 / |K_G0| and require the residual to carry variance before phi enters the certificate. Keep the O-star-relevance-weighted phi as the version with a route to information the count cannot supply, and report it beside the uniform one rather than as an optional secondary.
objections.settling_measurement: Partial rank correlation of phi_1 with its numerator at fixed |K_G0| on the pilot instances, plus the interquartile range of phi_r computed within (r, |K_G0|-decile) cells rather than within r.

objections.objection: AS WRITTEN, COLUMN 11 CANNOT BE COMPUTED, AND THE PRE-REGISTERED FALLBACK SENTENCE NAMES THE WRONG RETIREMENT. C-COUNT-A and C-COUNT-B are integers, not decisions, and the protocol asks for their 'decision agreement ... at every operating point of the audit arm's three-bucket score' without ever stating what decision an integer produces or what sweeps to make the operating points. There is no threshold, no mapping from a count to the three buckets, and no ROC. Separately, the fallback sentence is pre-committed as 'the framework is retired to a lemma about counting', but on the measured evidence the baseline that will win is not a count: it is separation, with rank correlation 0.695, or component_size, which classifies r = 1 at 78.0% with no knowledge at all. The honest retirement is 'a lemma about how far the treatment sits from the certified set inside its chain component', which is a different sentence, a different literature (the locality of O-star that the protocol already cites in A1 and A2), and a different remaining budget. A pre-registration that commits the wrong fallback has not actually pre-committed the paper.
objections.where: primary_table Block 2 column 11; A3 falsifiable_check (a) decision rule wording; and the 'what it would show if the framework is wrong' item (3)
objections.repair: Give every baseline in the ladder an explicit decision rule (a threshold on the statistic, swept to produce a genuine ROC against the audited three-bucket outcome) and say so in the column definition. Pre-register TWO distinct fallback sentences, one for the count family and one for the geometric family, and name in advance which rung of the ladder decides which, so the paper's retirement text is fixed before the ladder runs rather than chosen after it.
objections.settling_measurement: Publish the ROC and the operating-point table for each of B1 through B6 against the audited outcome, on the committed 831 and on the pilot, with the threshold sweep printed rather than described.

attacks.verdict: SURVIVES, BUT ONLY UNDER A STAGE-0 GATE IT DOES NOT CURRENTLY HAVE. Fixed-Frame Kappa-Ball is the most self-critical protocol on the board and its fixed denominator is the right invention, but on the attack axis it fails in a specific, checkable place: its entire vacuity apparatus is denominated in counts, and counts are measurably the wrong baseline. Recomputed from results/axisa3/instances.jsonl, r <= |K_G0| in 831 of 831 (definitional, since k_g0 IS |retractable_edges|), r = |K_G0| in 15, Spearman(r, |K_G0|) = 0.057 with p = 0.102, and min(s, |K_G0|) = s in 463 of 463 measurable instances, so the count never binds. Against that, a fifteen-line BFS already on the deployment path reproduces the certificate exactly on 636 of 831 (76.5%), on every instance of 10 of 25 networks, and to within one on 99.4% of the non-illustration corpus whose whole range is {1,2,3,4}; component_size alone, before any elicitation, classifies r = 1 at 78.0% against a 61.1% base. The differentiating population, where r beats the free rule by 2 or more, is 18 instances on 3 networks, and 13 sit in `paths`, the drawing the protocol's own illustration gate deletes from every headline: five instances on two networks survive outside T0. The flagship pi-hat inherits all of it, equalling kappa exactly on 61.1% of instances, and its spread test is passed by between-network variation in elicitation reliability with r pinned at 1. THE MODIFICATION REQUIRED, and it is a modification rather than a repair note: (1) replace C-COUNT-A/B with a free-statistic ladder B0 majority, B1 component_size, B2 separation-with-fallback, B3 min(s,|K_G0|), B4 |K_G0|, B5 |K|, B6 r, each with a declared decision rule and a swept threshold; (2) replace 'reproduces at every operating point' with a pre-registered equivalence margin on a paired contrast against B2, with UNDERPOWERED as a pre-committed third verdict and a rescue clause requiring the |diff| >= 2 sub-population to be both large enough and outcome-bearing outside T0; (3) promote that ladder to a BLOCKING Stage 0, run on the 831 committed rows and on the five-network D-LLM pilot before the 2,000-plus elicitations and 22 human-hours are released; (4) redefine D-NULL as a size- and placement-matched random consistent K, since K empty gives zero retractable edges and hence a column of UNREACHED sentinels by construction; (5) insert |K_G0|, the separation composition and the applicability funnel (767 of 9,771 edges, 969 of 7,062 nodes, 25 of 39 networks) into the certificate ledger ahead of the radius columns; (6) state pi-hat's spread conditional on r and against pi-hat(s). Items 1 through 3 are load-bearing: without them the protocol will deliver a real, well-audited, internally consistent result that a referee retires with a script that costs less than one elicitation call. The tell is that Fixed-Frame already found and printed the illustration finding, the single most damaging fact about its own range, and then wrote its baseline gate in a unit that cannot detect the consequence.

objections.objection: THE SPECIFIC LEAK. The frozen frame — the protocol's headline contribution — is a true-DAG functional, and the elicitation budget proves it cannot be otherwise. A2 defines the frame as 'X drawn from the nodes lying in or adjacent to a chain component of C-hat of size >= 2' and sizes it at '969 nodes of 7,062, in 276 components, on 33 networks'. I recomputed all four integers from results/axisa3/descriptive_structure.csv by summing over the 39 is_dag rows: n_nodes_in_components = 969, n_nodes = 7,062, n_components = 276, networks with n_components > 0 = 33. Every one is computed from the CPDAG of the TRUE DAG. So the fixed denominator every arm is read against is selected by the truth. The protocol cannot escape by re-deriving the frame per panel: (a) that unpairs P-ORACLE from P-EST and restores the composition confound the fixed denominator exists to kill, and (b) the budget forbids it. P-EST is 5 Pi points x 5 seeds = 25 estimated CPDAGs per network; elicitation is 'one query per chain component'; estimated CPDAGs have different chain components; so K must be re-elicited per (network, Pi, seed). The stated budget is '276 chain-component elicitations ... times 2 replicates, times 3 naming conditions' = 1,656, 'roughly 1,900 calls', with no Pi factor anywhere. It is right only if K is elicited ONCE on the ORACLE chain components and reused, which puts the true DAG on the deployment arm's K exactly as select_knowledge did. Worse, the elicitor's own signature is elicit(nodes, context) (src/bkrobust/knowledge/elicit.py:62): under one-query-per-component the PARTITION of variables into queries is the graph, so 'given variable names and a dataset card and never the graph' is false — the surrogate is handed the oracle CPDAG's chain-component partition, i.e. told exactly which orientations the data could not settle.
objections.where: A2 (frame + fixed denominator), A5 (two panels), arm D-LLM, budget line in A3
objections.repair: Build the frozen frame on an ESTIMATED C-hat: one designated reference discovery run at the largest Pi, with seed, CI test and alpha declared in the manifest, and the frame's provenance printed as C-hat_E. Run P-ORACLE on that same frozen instance list and report oracle-admissibility as a printed status, never as a filter — the same demotion the protocol already applies to K-dependent conditions, applied to the panel. Elicit K once, per component of that same reference C-hat_E, so the surrogate's variable partition is analyst-observable. Restate the elicitation budget with an explicit panel factor rather than leaving it at 1,900.
objections.settling_measurement: Compute the frame on the oracle C-hat and on the reference estimated C-hat at each Pi, and report per network (i) the Jaccard overlap of the two candidate-pair sets and (ii) the adjusted Rand index of the two chain-component partitions. The oracle side is already fixed (276 components, 969 nodes, 33 networks), so only the estimated side has to be run. Pre-register a floor; below it, no P-ORACLE row may be cited in support of any P-EST claim and the elicitation is repeated per panel with the budget restated.

objections.objection: The invariant is enforced on QUANTITIES; every leak in this protocol runs through DECISIONS, and the third manifest value is the laundering channel. The manifest carries arm in {deployment, audit, substrate_design} and true_dag_on_path in {false, via_Chat_only, true}, plus 'a check that refuses to publish when a deployment-tagged quantity carries anything but false'. That check is per-quantity and cannot see a deployment INPUT that was SET by a true-DAG statistic. There are at least five such decisions. (i) A1's THIRD RULE: 'any arm carrying continuous parameters showing var-sortability above 0.94 has its parameterisation replaced (iSCM ... or UUMC) before a single result is reported.' Var-sortability counts edges of the TRUE DAG whose tail has smaller marginal variance; the parameterisation it selects determines Sigma-hat; and the invariant's own equation is r(C-hat, K, X, Y, Sigma-hat, n). A truth-scored statistic therefore chooses a deployment input — under the tag arm = substrate_design, which the publish check waves through by construction. (ii) A3 check (c): networks flagged by an ACCURACY gap, which requires the truth, 'move to a separately reported stratum ... and are never pooled'. Pooling membership is the denominator of a deployment rate, so the fixed denominator — the protocol's headline contribution — acquires a truth-shaped hole. X-CONTAM says the accuracy flag 'may not restratify any deployment number'; A3's own decision rule then restratifies. (iii) Checkable #13: an audit-scored confidence-calibration curve licenses the deployment arm to read confidence, and on T3 there is no audit to fit it. (iv) A6-1 is 'CALIBRATED FIRST on K-SYN at a known corruption rate', where known means known against the true tier assignment. (v) Objection 1's frame.
objections.where: A6 (manifest and publish check), A1 third rule, A3 checkable #13 and check (c), A6-1
objections.repair: Replace the per-quantity flag with a DECISION LOG. Every parameter on r's computation path — the frame, the per-network cap, the parameterisation, denominator/pooling membership, whether confidence is read, which arms enter which headline — carries set_by: <statistic> and INHERITS that statistic's own true_dag_on_path. The publish check refuses when any deployment input's set_by chain does not terminate in false. This is the transitive-provenance idea generalised from data provenance to decision provenance, which is the generalisation Fixed-Frame needs and does not have. Where a decision genuinely must be taken on a truth-scored statistic (sortability is the honest case, because Reisach demands it), the rule is: take it, tag the whole arm via_substrate_choice, and forbid that arm from carrying a deployment headline — do not let substrate_design mean 'inert'.
objections.settling_measurement: Before any run, execute the publish-refusing check as a dry run against the protocol's own written decision rules and print how many refuse. Pre-registered prediction, in the protocol's two-stage discipline: at least the five above. If the check passes all five as written, it is not testing what it claims and must be rewritten rather than trusted.

objections.objection: THE SUBSTRATE PINCER: no tier can carry the sentence the LLM arm exists to license. T0 is the dagitty tutorial set (confounding, mediator, paths, M-bias) — canonical teaching material, maximally memorised, and by the protocol's own illustration gate never pooled into a headline. T1 is the 24 BIF networks, of which ASIA, ALARM, CHILD, INSURANCE and SACHS sit in published LLM-plus-SCM evaluation sets; A3 check (c) itself concedes that if more than half of T1 lands flagged, 'the surrogate arm is a contamination measurement rather than an expertise measurement on the benchmark tier'. T2 is the 8 author-named applied DAGs — and D-PUB, the only human-produced referent on the whole board, is harvested FROM THOSE SAME EIGHT PAPERS. So on any contaminated T2 network D-LLM and D-PUB are not two samples; they are one source read twice, once by a model and once by a human. A6-1's null (K-LLM resembles K-PUB) is then trivially true, and a non-rejection would be reported as evidence of realism when it is evidence of shared provenance. T3 is where A-TWIN is 'absent on every T3 row' by construction, so the tier closest to deployment has no verification at all. The protocol's fallback chain runs T1 -> 'the realism claim rests on K-PUB' -> a tier it has already declared underpowered by its own arithmetic (~160 instances against a McNemar requirement of ~455, short by a factor of 2.8). Every exit is closed, and it is closed by facts the protocol itself states in four separate places without ever putting them side by side.
objections.where: A1 tiers x A6-4 contamination x A6-2 power x A-TWIN's T3 absence; arms D-LLM and D-PUB
objections.repair: Two parts, both cheap. (a) A SOURCE-OVERLAP PROBE, scored against the PAPER rather than the truth and therefore fully deployment-legal: ask each model cold, from the variable list alone, to name the source publication and reproduce its declared exposure, outcome and adjustment set. The corpus supplies the answer key for free — the dagitty attrs group this protocol already restores carries 12 exposures, 12 outcomes and 3 adjusted nodes (Didelez_2010: Age, Smo; Thoemmes_2013: s2). Any network where the model returns the paper's own exposure/outcome pair above chance is declared SINGLE-SOURCE, A6-1 is void there and printed as void, and D-PUB is not a second sample on it. (b) Strike 'LLM-as-expert surrogate' and every practice-facing sentence from the protocol, and rename the arm what it can actually be: a mechanical knowledge source with a measured, prompt-dependent error process. Restore the word 'expert' only when a post-cutoff or newly drawn tier exists.
objections.settling_measurement: Run the source-overlap probe over all 12 dagitty files and the 24 BIF networks, two model families, cold, no data — roughly 72 cached calls. It decides whether the T2 fallback the whole design leans on when T1 is flagged exists at all, and it costs hours, not weeks.

objections.objection: D-TRUE and D-SYN sit in the deployment block with oracle-derived K, and the protocol's own publish check would refuse eight of its seventeen deployment rows. D-TRUE's 'K is drawn from true orientations only'. D-SYN starts from D-TRUE's K, corrupts it against the TRUE temporal tier, and reports 'realised post-filter wrongness recorded separately from intended' — a truth-scored quantity. Both carry the D- prefix, both are named among 'the five deployment arms LLM, PUB (T2 only), TRUE, SYN, NULL: seventeen rows', and Block 1's header stamp reads 'arm = deployment, true_dag_on_path = false'. Four tiers x two arms = eight of those seventeen rows are oracle-derived. A-ORACLE is correctly flagged true and correctly greyed; D-TRUE and D-SYN are the same object with a different prefix. This is precisely the failure a per-quantity flag cannot catch, because breakdown_radius takes no DAG in its signature and every quantity on r's argument list is observable — only K's PROVENANCE carries the truth. The protocol's one-sentence defence of D-LLM ('Every quantity on its computation path is a functional of (C-hat, K, X, Y, Sigma-hat, n)') is equally true of D-TRUE, which is exactly why the defence does not work.
objections.where: arms D-TRUE and D-SYN; primary table Block 1 (seventeen deployment rows)
objections.repair: Propagate the flag over K's provenance rather than over r's arguments. Add a fourth true_dag_on_path value via_K. Move D-TRUE and D-SYN below the horizontal rule alongside A-ORACLE and N-ER-MATCHED, and relabel them A-TRUE and A-SYN. Their scientific roles are untouched — A-TRUE remains the size- and placement-matched true control without which every false-knowledge comparison is confounded with claim count, A-SYN remains A6-1's known-error-process calibration input — only their block changes. Nothing in the design is lost and the invariant stops being a paragraph.
objections.settling_measurement: Run the publish-refusing check with K-provenance propagation over a dry-run manifest of the seventeen rows before any data is generated. Predicted refusals: eight. If it refuses fewer, the propagation is not implemented and the check is decorative.

objections.objection: kappa-hat_split is a LOWER BOUND presented as the referent, and one arm of its pre-registered decision rule is uninterpretable by construction — in the dangerous direction. The arithmetic is sound and needs no independence: if two elicitations disagree on an assertion, at least one is wrong, so the average error over the pair is at least delta/2. But the protocol substitutes that bound into pi-hat = 1 - (1 - kappa-hat)^r and then reads the result in BOTH directions: 'if pi-hat exceeds 0.9 on more than 90% of instances the certificate never survives ... if it falls below 0.1 on more than 90% the referent is too small to threaten anything.' A lower bound on kappa yields a lower bound on pi. The high arm is therefore a valid refutation; the low arm is vacuous, because two elicitations that AGREE may both be wrong in the same way — which is exactly what a shared pretraining prior produces, and exactly the failure mode the contamination screen exists to detect. So the protocol's only reassuring outcome is the one its statistic cannot support, and a contaminated surrogate that recites the same wrong published orientation twice returns delta = 0, pi-hat = 0, and a certificate that reads maximally safe. The protocol's own weakness list admits the slack is unmeasured; it never repairs it, and it never measures the slack on the tiers where A-TWIN could.
objections.where: A6 calibration (pi-hat), arm D-LLM', primary table Block 1 columns 7 and 9
objections.repair: Three parts. (i) Print pi_lo only, and pre-register that a low pi_lo is reported UNINFORMATIVE, never as evidence of a surviving certificate. (ii) Measure the slack where it can be measured: on every A-TWIN-audited instance compute s = kappa_true / (delta/2) and report its distribution with between-network dispersion. (iii) Pre-register that no truth-free tier may carry the breach column unless s's interquartile range on T1 and T2 sits inside a declared factor, and print that factor in the caption. This is the bridge check the sibling protocol ships for its own oracle-free referent; Fixed-Frame has the identical transfer problem and no check at all.
objections.settling_measurement: The s distribution on the audited tiers, with its between-network variance tested against the sampling variance implied by each network's assertion count. If s is statistically a constant, use one declared global scalar and say so. If its IQR spans more than the declared factor of two, the T3 rows lose their breach column and the paper says why.

objections.objection: kappa-hat_split measures the INSTRUMENT, not the analyst, and the replicate design is chosen after looking, so the column is two statistics under one header. D-LLM' varies 'the prompt's variable-order permutation seed' — precisely the mention-order bias the ledger records as a documented, systematic LLM artefact that persists on controlled synthetic data. So the certificate's referent is denominated in the elicitation interface's own instability. Two consequences. First, the one-sentence pitch — 'the disagreement your own two elicitations already exhibit' — is not available to a practitioner, who has one expert and no variable-order seed; the quantity does not exist outside this instrument, so no practice-facing sentence can be written from it. Second, the protocol rewards hiding the risk: an order-invariant prompt, or averaging over orders, mechanically lowers delta, lowers pi-hat and makes every certificate look safer, with no change whatever to how wrong the knowledge is. Then A6's fourth rule adapts the design after seeing the statistic: 'if kappa-hat_split is zero or near-zero ... the replicate must vary the model family instead.' Some networks' kappa then comes from order seeds and others' from two vendors, chosen post hoc on the value of the very number being calibrated. The 'spread' that A6's third rule pre-registers as the informative outcome can be produced entirely by which replicate design each network happened to end up with.
objections.where: arm D-LLM'; A3 (five paraphrase/order replicates); A6 fourth decision rule
objections.repair: Decompose delta before it is used, and forbid post-hoc switching. Report delta_instrument (same model, two order seeds) and delta_source (two model families) as SEPARATE columns on every row, and pre-register that only delta_source enters pi-hat while delta_instrument is reported as an instrument-stability column. Add a third component wherever a human referent exists: have D-PUB's harvest adjudicated by two independent coders rather than one adjudicator, and report delta_human on the same scale. That also converts the harvest from a task with no counterparty into one with a waiting second reader, which is the only change that makes it likely to happen.
objections.settling_measurement: The three deltas on the eight T2 networks, on the same assertions. Pre-registered prediction under the two-stage discipline: delta_instrument >= delta_source. If it holds, the referent as written is an instrument property and the certificate is priced in units of prompt sensitivity, which must be said in the abstract rather than the appendix.

objections.objection: pi-hat is a relabelling of kappa-hat on the majority of the table, and the observed radius range cannot produce the spread the decision rule calls the informative outcome. pi-hat = 1 - (1 - kappa)^r equals kappa EXACTLY at r = 1. Recomputed from results/axisa3/instances.jsonl: r = 1 on 508 of 831 admissible instances (61.1%), r <= 2 on 768 (92.4%); outside the T0 illustrations r >= 2 holds on 304 of 807 (37.7%) and the maximum radius is 4, with all 16 instances at r >= 5 in `paths`. So on three fifths of the rows the breach column is the referent column with a new name, and on 92% of rows pi-hat takes one of exactly two values at fixed kappa. At kappa = 0.10 those two values are 0.100 and 0.190, a spread of 0.09; meanwhile a between-network kappa varying over a plausible 0.05 to 0.30 gives a spread of 0.25 at r = 1 alone — nearly three times as wide. The pre-registered 'informative spread' is therefore dominated by between-network variation in the surrogate's self-disagreement, and the protocol would report a successful calibration in a world where r is constant. That is the same category of finding as the protocol's own illustration gate, turned on its own headline column.
objections.where: A6 calibration; primary table Block 1 column 9
objections.repair: At r = 1 print kappa-hat itself with the plain sentence that the certificate offers zero safe moves there, and reserve pi-hat for r >= 2 with that sub-population's size printed per tier. Add the partial correlation of pi-hat with r holding kappa-hat fixed as a first-class column, and restrict A6's third decision rule (the spread criterion) to the r >= 2 rows.
objections.settling_measurement: That partial correlation on the r >= 2 rows, with a cluster bootstrap over networks. If it is not distinguishable from zero at the realised n, pi-hat carries no information the referent does not, the certificate ledger's headline column is a restatement, and the paper says so rather than printing two columns that are one number.

objections.objection: The named-versus-scrambled AGREEMENT rate is uninterpretable in both directions, and it is the deployment arm's ONLY contamination column. The protocol correctly moves the truth-requiring accuracy gap into the audit block, then gives the deployment arm 'the truth-free twin, the named-versus-scrambled AGREEMENT rate between two elicitations'. Consider what that rate can take. Agreement is HIGH when the model ignores names and answers from a structural or lexical heuristic — no contamination and no knowledge, the vacuous case. Agreement is LOW when the answer depends on the names, which is true BOTH when the model recites a memorised published graph AND when it reasons correctly from domain semantics. So the column takes the same value under the arm working and under the arm reciting, and the opposite value under the arm being vacuous. Its sign is not merely ambiguous, it is inverted relative to what a reader will assume. A6-4 concedes the underlying point verbatim ('the accuracy gap bounds memorisation from above and domain knowledge from below without separating them') and keeps the truth-free version of the same broken contrast anyway, in the block where nothing can correct it.
objections.where: arm X-CONTAM, A6-4, primary table Block 1 (the deployment-arm contamination column)
objections.repair: Replace it with a STRUCTURE-DEPENDENCE probe, which is truth-free, needs no scrambling, and runs on every tier including T3 where no audit exists. Elicit twice on the same real names: once with the chain component presented as it is, and once with the presented component perturbed so that a correct answer must change (one adjacency deleted, one spurious adjacency added, both drawn from C-hat under a declared seed). Report the fraction of assertions UNCHANGED. A model reasoning from the data-derived structure changes its answer; a model reciting a published graph does not. High invariance is a contamination signal with one unambiguous sign, it is a functional of C-hat and two elicitations only, and it costs one extra pass on an already-budgeted cache.
objections.settling_measurement: The structure-dependence rate per network, against a floor calibrated on perturbations where the correct answer provably changes (available from A-SYN, in the audit block, without touching the deployment number). If the surrogate's invariance on T1 is indistinguishable from its invariance when the presented structure is randomised, K is not a function of the data at all and the deployment arm is reporting recall.

objections.objection: The recitation check's chance level is a single scalar applied to a query family whose answer spaces run from 2 to 85 factorial. A3 check (c) states 'Chance on a triplet-order query over three nodes is one in six.' But the elicitation unit is not a triplet; A3's own decision is 'one query per chain component', and the corpus's components are wildly heterogeneous. Recomputed from instances.jsonl over the 831 admissible instances, X's chain component has size 2 in 169 of them (20.3%), size 3 in 137, size 4 in 142, size 11 in 160, and size 85 in 2. A size-2 component is a single undirected edge whose causal-order query has exactly two answers, so chance is 1/2 and not 1/6; pathfinder's 85-node component has a chance level indistinguishable from zero. And the admissible answer space is not m! but the Meek-consistent subset of it given C-hat, which is smaller still and varies per component. A single scalar null therefore mis-sizes the flag in both directions across the table — and by objection 2(ii) that flag decides which networks are pooled into a deployment headline, so a mis-sized null propagates into a deployment denominator.
objections.where: A3 falsifiable check (c), the recitation flag; feeds A6-4 and the pooling rule
objections.repair: Compute the chance level PER COMPONENT as the fraction of orderings consistent with C-hat restricted to that component — exact enumeration where the component is small, uniform sampling of Meek-consistent orientations otherwise. This is a functional of C-hat alone, so it is deployment-legal, it is cheap on a corpus whose 276 components average 3.5 nodes, and it makes the binomial bound the protocol already wants correctly sized. Print the per-component null beside every flag.
objections.settling_measurement: Publish the per-component chance distribution and report how many networks change flag status between the 1/6 null and the per-component null. Any network that changes was mis-flagged, and under objection 2(ii) any deployment rate whose denominator depended on that flag was mis-stated.

objections.objection: A6-1's power calibration is against ONE alternative and is then reported as a scalar verdict. The rule reads: 'a two-sample discriminator that cannot separate D-SYN at 0.50 from D-TRUE has no power and its verdict on the real sources means nothing.' That is a necessary condition dressed as a sufficient one. Power is not a scalar property of a test; it is a property of a test against a specific alternative. D-SYN's tiered misfiling produces error that is spatially clustered BY CONSTRUCTION — 'one mistake flips several claims at once' — and spatial clustering is one named coordinate of the pre-registered feature vector ('pairwise graph distance among wrong assertions'). Establishing power against clustered error therefore establishes power on the one coordinate D-SYN was built to move, and says nothing about power against an alternative that differs in the distance-from-X profile, the granularity mix, or the commission/omission ratio — which is precisely where LLM error is most likely to differ from a temporal-tier misfiling. A protocol that then reports 'not distinguishable' as a single verdict will read a coordinate-specific blind spot as evidence of realism.
objections.where: A6-1 discriminator; arm D-SYN as its calibration input
objections.repair: Calibrate on a FAMILY of single-coordinate alternatives, one per feature in the pre-registered vector, each perturbing that coordinate alone at a declared effect size, and report a per-coordinate minimum detectable effect. A non-rejection is then reported coordinate by coordinate — 'not distinguishable on cascade size at d >= x, on distance-from-X at d >= y' — never as one verdict. Keep D-SYN as the clustered-error alternative it genuinely is, and stop letting it stand for all alternatives.
objections.settling_measurement: Print the per-coordinate MDE table beside every A6-1 result. On the protocol's own tier sizes (8 harvestable networks, paired sign-flip permutation, floor 2/2^8) the prediction is that several coordinates have no resolvable effect at all; those are named in the caption rather than absorbed into a null.

objections.objection: kappa-hat_RoCA compares a test statistic across models with different degrees of freedom, so it measures the size of the comparison rather than the credibility of the assertion. The definition is: 'for each k in K let G_{-k} = Meek(C-hat, K minus {k}) and let T be the over-identification statistic on (X, Y, Sigma-hat, n); kappa-hat_RoCA is the fraction of the analyst's own assertions whose retraction lowers T.' Retracting an assertion re-opens part of a chain component and therefore changes how many valid adjustment sets G0 admits. Su and Henckel's statistic is a chi-squared over-identification statistic on stacked OLS coefficients whose degrees of freedom scale with the number of compared sets. So 'retraction lowers T' conflates 'this assertion was wrong' with 'retraction reduced the count of compared sets and hence the df' — and the second is by far the more common event, since re-opening a component is what retraction does. As written, one of the protocol's three observable referents is a df artefact, and it is the one used on exactly the sub-population where the incumbent test has power.
objections.where: A6 (kappa-hat_RoCA), comparator arm C-ROCA, A2 item 7 (valid-set count)
objections.repair: Compare p-values under each model's own degrees of freedom, or standardise T by its df, and pre-register that instances where retraction CHANGES the valid-set count are reported in their own stratum rather than pooled. The count is already available at no extra cost: A2 item 7 records the number of valid adjustment sets with an early exit at 2, which is exactly the quantity needed to detect the df change.
objections.settling_measurement: Report the joint distribution of (Delta T, Delta df) over all retractions. If the sign of Delta T is predicted by Delta df alone at better than chance, kappa-hat_RoCA as written is a df artefact and must be replaced by the standardised version before it enters any table.

objections.objection: Temperature 0 plus a mandatory shared cache can make kappa-hat_split identically zero as an implementation accident, and the protocol's fourth decision rule then fires on a bug. Both D-LLM' and X-CONTAM fix 'temperature 0, mandatory response cache'. The two deployment replicates differ ONLY in the variable-order permutation seed, so they are two distinct elicitations only if the cache key includes the rendered prompt text after permutation, rather than a normalised, semantic or component-identity key. If the key is normalised in any way, replicate two is a cache hit, delta is identically zero on every instance, pi-hat is identically zero, and A6's fourth rule routes a perfectly functioning protocol into the contamination branch — or, worse, the zero is read as 'the surrogate is deterministic' and the design is adaptively switched to the model-family replicate for the wrong reason (objection 6). The same key must also keep X-CONTAM's three naming conditions from serving responses to D-LLM's single pass.
objections.where: arm D-LLM', arm X-CONTAM, A3 checkable #12 (provenance and cache)
objections.repair: State the cache key in the manifest as (model id, hash of the rendered prompt after permutation, naming condition, replicate seed), and add a startup assertion that two replicates of the same chain component produce two distinct keys. Print the cache-hit count per arm in the manifest.
objections.settling_measurement: A unit test asserting distinct keys, plus the printed per-arm cache-hit count. A cache-hit count equal to the replicate count is a failed run and must be reported as such, never as a null result on kappa-hat_split.

objections.objection: The status vocabulary has no cell for the most likely P-EST outcome, so the one column that makes the arms comparable would misreport. The fixed denominator's statuses are ok / knowledge_inconsistent / o_g0_not_identified / o_g0_empty / z_invalid_at_g0 / budget_censored. Under P-EST the estimated C-hat's skeleton differs from the one K was elicited against — that is the whole point of running an estimated panel — so a live and expected outcome is an assertion about a node pair that C-hat_E does not carry as an undirected edge at all. Meek Algorithm 1 does not necessarily return FAIL on such an assertion: it is not a graphical inconsistency, it is an assertion about a non-edge. The instance would therefore land silently in ok, or in an inconsistency bucket it does not belong to, and the status-composition column — the protocol's single best invention — would misreport exactly on the panel that is the only one allowed to carry a deployment claim.
objections.where: A2 item 3 (fixed denominator status vocabulary), A5 (P-EST)
objections.repair: Add k_refers_to_non_edge and k_partially_applicable to the status vocabulary before the run, with the count of dropped or inapplicable assertions recorded per instance. Apply the same discipline the protocol applies everywhere else — a condition becomes a printed status, never a silent filter — to the one case its own two-panel design creates.
objections.settling_measurement: The per-panel distribution of that status. It is also the cheapest available measurement of how far an oracle-elicited K is from being usable on an estimated graph, which is the transfer that objection 1's repair rests on, so it should be run on the pilot five networks before the elicitation budget is committed.

attacks.verdict:
SURVIVES, BUT NOT AS AN LLM-AS-EXPERT PROTOCOL AND NOT WITH THE FRAME IT HAS. Six changes are load-bearing; without the first two the protocol's own invariant fails on its own headline contribution.

(1) THE FRAME MOVES TO AN ESTIMATED C-HAT. The frozen candidate frame is sized at "969 nodes of 7,062, in 276 components, on 33 networks" — I recomputed all four integers from results/axisa3/descriptive_structure.csv and every one is a functional of the CPDAG of the TRUE DAG. The fixed denominator, the thing that makes D-NULL, D-TRUE, D-SYN and D-LLM comparable at all, is selected by the truth. The escape (re-derive per panel) is closed twice: it unpairs P-ORACLE from P-EST and restores the composition confound the fixed denominator exists to kill, and the elicitation budget forbids it — P-EST is 5 Pi x 5 seeds = 25 estimated CPDAGs per network, elicitation is one query per chain component, and the stated 1,900 calls (276 x 2 x 3 = 1,656) carries no Pi factor anywhere. The budget is only correct if K is elicited once on the ORACLE chain components and reused, which puts the true DAG on the deployment arm's K exactly as select_knowledge did. This is the specific leak.

(2) THE MANIFEST BECOMES A DECISION LOG. The invariant is enforced on quantities; every leak here runs through decisions, and `substrate_design` is the laundering channel. Var-sortability is a true-DAG functional, and A1's third rule uses it to choose the parameterisation, which sets Sigma-hat, which is a deployment input by the invariant's own equation r(C-hat, K, X, Y, Sigma-hat, n). A truth-scored accuracy flag decides which networks are pooled, i.e. the denominator of a deployment rate. An audit-fitted calibration curve licenses the deployment arm to read confidence. A6-1 is calibrated on a corruption defined against the true tier assignment. Every deployment input needs set_by provenance that inherits its setter's true_dag_on_path, and the publish check must refuse on the chain, not the leaf.

(3) D-TRUE AND D-SYN MOVE BELOW THE RULE. Eight of the seventeen deployment rows carry oracle-derived K under a header stamped true_dag_on_path = false. Cheap to fix, fatal to leave.

(4) KAPPA-HAT_SPLIT IS DEMOTED FROM REFERENT TO FLOOR. It is a lower bound read in both directions; the reassuring half is vacuous, and a contaminated surrogate that recites the same wrong orientation twice returns delta = 0 and a maximally safe certificate. It also measures the instrument (order-permutation sensitivity) rather than the analyst, and the replicate design is switched post hoc on the statistic's own value, so the column is two quantities under one header. Decompose into delta_instrument and delta_source, let only delta_source price the certificate, and measure the slack s = kappa_true/(delta/2) on the audited tiers before any T3 row carries a breach column. And note that at r = 1 — 61.1% of the committed corpus, 92.4% at r <= 2, maximum radius 4 outside T0 — pi-hat IS kappa-hat, so the pre-registered "informative spread" is dominated by between-network surrogate disagreement (0.25 at plausible kappa) rather than by the radius (0.09 across r in {1,2}).

(5) THE NAMED-VS-SCRAMBLED COLUMN IS REPLACED. Its value is identical under "the surrogate is reciting" and "the surrogate is working," and inverted under "the surrogate is vacuous." The structure-dependence probe (same names, perturbed presented component, fraction of assertions unchanged) is truth-free, unambiguous in sign, and available on T3 where nothing else is.

(6) "EXPERT SURROGATE" IS STRUCK UNTIL A TIER EXISTS THAT CAN CARRY IT. The substrate pincer is complete: T0 is tutorial material the protocol's own gate excludes from headlines; T1 is the BIF corpus whose famous members sit in published LLM evaluation sets; T2 is circular, because D-PUB is harvested from the same eight papers the surrogate may have read, so A6-1's null is trivially true under contamination and a non-rejection would be reported as realism; T3 has no audit twin by construction. The source-overlap probe (cold recall of the paper's own exposure/outcome/adjusted set, scored against the paper and not the truth, ~72 calls) is the cheapest thing on the board and it decides whether the T2 fallback exists at all.

WHAT SURVIVES UNTOUCHED AND IS THE REAL CONTRIBUTION: the fixed denominator as a REPORTING discipline (K-dependent conditions as printed statuses, not filters) — which is right even though its instance list is currently oracle-derived; the illustration gate, which I verified fires on committed data (all 16 instances at r >= 5 are in `paths`, and the maximum radius over the remaining 807 is 4); the retraction-subset shell measure, which is the only implementable one on a poset whose covering relation has no known graphical characterisation; the four comparator arms run on our own instances; the derived per-network cap; and the honest pre-declaration that D-PUB is underpowered. Repaired on the six points above, the protocol is the strongest on the board. Unrepaired on points 1 and 2, it reproduces the defect it was designed to remove, one level up.

SURVIVES, but only with its numeric layer rebuilt before any threshold is committed — and the rebuild must be the FIRST thing that runs, because the protocol's own two-stage discipline requires thresholds to be fixed before the data are seen, and four of its thresholds are currently derived from constants that files already on disk contradict.

The design is the strongest on the board and none of what follows touches it: the fixed denominator with status composition, the C-hat-only frame (the only one that stays paired across knowledge arms), the breach probability replacing an arithmetically dead credibility ratio, and the illustration gate as a self-hostile check are all correct and should be kept verbatim. What will not survive an audit is the reporting form the design is presented in. Concretely, and each recomputed from /Users/josecosta/bkrobust/results/axisa3/ today:

(1) THE TAIL IS AN INSTRUMENT BOUNDARY, NOT A SUBSTRATE FACT. src/bkrobust/hybrid.py sets DEFAULT_SEARCH_BUDGET = 3 and dispatches to a second estimator when the bounded search exhausts it. Measured: local_up_fast answered 811 instances with radii strictly in {1,2,3}; e1_ladder answered 20 with radii strictly in {4..14}. `method` is a deterministic function of the answer, switching at exactly 3/4 — which is exactly where the illustration gate reads. Every sentence of the form "max r outside T0 is 4", "zero outside T0 at r >= 5", "94.4% at r <= 2" is a statement about a two-estimator mixture with no column recording which leg answered.

(2) THE FRAME ARITHMETIC IS 3x INFLATED AND ITS UNIVERSE IS A 0.73% UNEQUAL-PROBABILITY SUBSAMPLE. 115,974 is 3 x 38,658 distinct pairs; the coverage-independent rejections are each exactly 3x their distinct value (verified 22,110 / 14,206 / 1,246 / 553 at every coverage). The candidate bracket "7,026 to 49,644" is exactly 3 x (2,342 to 16,548). And 38,658 is itself a per-network sample of 5,272,642 ordered pairs at inclusion rates from 1.000 (asia, insurance, barley) to 0.00037 (munin3: 400 of 1,082,640), with no weighting anywhere.

(3) THREE THRESHOLDS ARE SET AGAINST VALUES THE CORPUS REFUTES. Assumed ICC 0.1 against a measured 0.398 (r=1) and 0.544 (separation); an 11.1-point r=1 decision threshold against a 35.0-point cluster-bootstrap interval on the same quantity; a 40% pilot admissibility gate against 31.4% and 28.1% in the corpus's own partial-knowledge cells.

(4) THE TWO COST FACTS HAVE NO COMMITTED ARTEFACT. The string 1,839.78 appears nowhere in ~/bkrobust; probe.log is one line in the vault, n = 1, and the call it timed is is_valid_adjustment_set_mpdag(cpdag, ...) — the CPDAG with K empty, not G0.

REQUIRED MODIFICATION: insert an ARM-0 RECOMPUTATION PASS ahead of everything, which (a) re-derives every constant from instances.jsonl and publishes the derivation next to the constant, (b) declares one canonical machine-written numbers file and stamps every printed number with artefact + JSON key, (c) adds three columns to the certificate ledger — dispatch leg, per-network inclusion probability, dispersion kind — and (d) restates every decision rule as a paired within-instance contrast with clustering on both sides. Without that pass the protocol will produce a fifth set of circulating figures that disagree with the four already committed, which is the exact failure it was designed to end.

objections.objection: THE RADIUS TAIL IS A SEARCH-DISPATCH ARTEFACT, AND THE ILLUSTRATION GATE READS EXACTLY ON THE BOUNDARY. /Users/josecosta/bkrobust/src/bkrobust/hybrid.py sets DEFAULT_SEARCH_BUDGET = 3; breakdown_radius runs radius_local_up_fast to that depth and falls through to radius_e1 only when the budget is exhausted. So `method` is a deterministic function of the answer. Recomputed from results/axisa3/instances.jsonl: local_up_fast answered 811 admissible instances with radii strictly in {1,2,3} (508/260/43); e1_ladder answered 20 with radii strictly in {4,...,14}. NO instance answered by the bounded search ever exceeded 3, and NO instance answered by the ladder was ever below 4. The illustration gate keys on r >= 3 and r >= 5 and concludes 'the certificate's measured range on real structure is {1,2,3,4}'. That range is a mixture of two estimators whose switch point sits at 3/4, and the primary table has no column for which leg answered. The confound is perfect and three-deep: all 16 instances at r >= 5 are simultaneously (a) in one network, (b) e1_ladder-answered, and (c) at coverage 1.0 where G0 IS the true DAG with k_g0 = 14 = all of that network's orientable edges. The gate attributes the tail to (a) alone, on a 16-row population, and calls it a substrate finding.
objections.where: A1 falsifiable_check, SECOND RULE (the illustration gate); A4 unit table; the primary table's column 4 (max r printed twice)
objections.repair: Three changes. (i) Add `dispatch_leg` to the per-instance record and print it as a column of the certificate ledger next to r; no max-radius or r-share sentence may be written over a mixture without it. (ii) Re-run the corpus with search_budget set at or above max |K_G0| per instance (median 10, max 122, so budget = |K_G0| is affordable at the polynomial gate's 1.07 ms) so that NO instance dispatches to the ladder, and report the radius distribution under a single estimator. (iii) Where the ladder is still needed, run a two-leg differential on the instances where both terminate and publish the disagreement rate WITH ITS SIGN, exactly as the fast_gate precedent required. Then restate the illustration gate over three strata and not one: with T0, without T0, and by dispatch leg.
objections.settling_measurement: On results/axisa3/instances.jsonl: `max(radius) by method` returns 3 for local_up_fast (n=811) and min 4 for e1_ladder (n=20) — already dispositive that the strata are separated by the instrument. The settling run is the single-estimator re-run: if under budget = |K_G0| some non-T0 network produces r >= 5, the gate's pre-registered claim ('zero outside T0 at r >= 5, already true in the committed corpus') is refuted and the substrate reading is withdrawn. If no non-T0 instance exceeds 3 under the uniform estimator, the honest range is {1,2,3} and even the '4' is a Kampen_2014 ladder row.

objections.objection: THE FRAME ARITHMETIC COUNTS COVERAGE-REPLICATED ROWS AS CANDIDATE PAIRS, AND THE SCREENING UNIVERSE IS MISSTATED BY A FACTOR OF 136. A2's cost block reads: 'Of 115,974 ordered pairs screened, 66,330 fail the X-side component test, leaving 49,644 whose X the frame proposes; the true-descendant filter then removed 42,618, so the frame yields between 7,026 and 49,644 candidates.' Recomputed: instances.jsonl holds 115,974 non-meta rows over only 38,658 DISTINCT (network, x, y) pairs, each screened at coverage 1.0, 0.5 and 0.25. The coverage-independent filters fire identically at each level — 22,110 / 14,206 / 1,246 / 553 per coverage — so 66,330, 42,618, 3,738 and 1,659 are each exactly 3x a distinct-pair count. The correct bracket is 2,342 to 16,548, and 7,026 = 3 x 2,342 and 49,644 = 3 x 16,548 confirm the arithmetic is uniformly tripled. Worse, 38,658 is not the universe either: summing total_ordered_pairs over the 39 _meta rows at coverage 1.0 gives 5,272,642, and fourteen networks were subsampled at rates from 0.62 down to 0.00037 (munin3: 400 of 1,082,640; munin/munin2/munin4/link all at or below 0.001). So every pair-weighted number in circulation is a design-weighted estimate over inclusion probabilities spanning three and a half orders of magnitude, with no weights recorded and no inverse-probability correction anywhere.
objections.where: A2 cost block and the frame-size derivation; the per-network _meta schema; the primary table's column 1 (instances / networks, both weights)
objections.repair: (i) Divide every rejection census by the number of coverage levels before it is used as a pair count, and print the distinct-pair census (22,110 / 14,206 / 1,246 / 553 / 543+182+106) as the canonical one. (ii) Add `inclusion_probability` to the per-network _meta row and print it as a column; a pair-weighted aggregate is then either Horvitz-Thompson weighted by 1/pi or explicitly labelled 'unweighted over a design-unequal sample' in its caption. (iii) Since the cap of 20 makes each network contribute equally, promote the network-weighted figure to the headline and demote the pair-weighted one to a diagnostic, which also removes the reason the two currently differ (45.4 vs 35.6 on separation, 61.1 vs 71.3 on r=1).
objections.settling_measurement: Recount instances.jsonl: len(set((network,x,y))) = 38,658 against 115,974 rows, and Counter(reject_reason) restricted to coverage 1.0 returns 22,110 / 14,206 / 1,246 / 553 / 543. Sum total_ordered_pairs over the coverage-1.0 _meta rows = 5,272,642. If the frame is re-derived on distinct pairs and the bracket comes back 2,342 to 16,548, every downstream cost, cap and power figure in A2 and A6 must be recomputed on the smaller number.

objections.objection: THE CAP AND EVERY POWER NUMBER ARE DERIVED FROM AN INTRACLASS CORRELATION OF 0.1 THAT THE COMMITTED FILE CONTRADICTS AT 0.398. A2 item (6) writes: 'with an intra-cluster correlation of 0.1 the design effect is 1 + (m-1) x 0.1, so m = 20 gives 2.9'. That 0.1 is asserted, not measured. One-way ANOVA on the r=1 indicator over the 25 yielding networks in instances.jsonl gives rho = 0.3978 (k=25, N=831, m0=30.51, MSB=3.179, MSW=0.150); on the separation >= 2 indicator over the full 831 it gives 0.5443. At rho = 0.398 the design effect at m = 20 is 1 + 19 x 0.398 = 8.56, not 2.9. Every power number in the protocol is multiplied by that factor and both of them invert: the necessity check's '172 effective observations x 2.9 = about 500 truly-invalid instances required' becomes about 1,472; A6-2's 'McNemar 157 x 2.9 = 455, short by a factor of 2.8' becomes 1,344, short by 8.4x. Worse, the effective sample is ceilinged by the number of networks, n_eff -> k/rho = 25/0.398 = 62.8, so no cap and no additional pair sampling on this corpus can reach even the 172 the declared half-width requires. objections.objection: THE BREACH PROBABILITY IS A MONOTONE RELABELLING OF KAPPA ON 92% OF THE CORPUS, AND IT IS THE ONE HEADLINE COLUMN WITH NO INTERVAL. pi-hat = 1 - (1 - kappa)^r.
